value.first: For a just-turned-2.5 girl, I'd do the 3-Day Method - an intensive weekend where diapers end and she goes bare-bottomed at home to learn her own body signals. It works because diapers hide the feeling of being wet; a focused block lets a ready child link the urge to action fast. First check she's ready: dry for 2 hours or after naps, notices when she's going, can sit steadily and pull pants down.
value.second: Prep: pick 3 clear days at home, put a potty in the room you live in, stock salty snacks and drinks she loves. Don't start if she's constipated or a big change is landing. Day 1: bag up the diapers together, "your pee and poop go in the potty now," naked below the waist all day. Push fluids so there are lots of tries. The moment pee starts, calmly carry her to the potty mid-stream and celebrate anything that lands. Nap and night in a pull-up - nights come later.
value.third: Every accident, flat and warm: "Pee goes in the potty, let's clean up together." Never scold. Day 2 add a short outing commando; Day 3 a longer one. Then stay commando for a few weeks. Expect "pees with prompting," not done - accidents run for weeks, and poop lags pee. If no poop for 3+ days or she's straining on hard, painful stools, that's a doctor call. If you can't clear 3 days, the gradual child-led approach works at her pace. I'll check in Thursday.
